subject: Re: Renewal & scale commitment — Highcrest
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Marsh <elena@highcrest.io>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal & scale commitment — Highcrest

Hi Elena,

Quick note to reconnect on your upcoming renewal (July 31). We heard from Omar that Highcrest expects a 2-3x during peak season next year and you may run a side-by-side with another vendor. I wanted to propose a straightforward path so we don’t slow your launch:

- 12-month renewal with an optional committed uplift (50% lower unit price when committing 6 months of upfront capacity).
- Short 48-hour side-by-side benchmark we’ll run with your sample workload; Redwood covers compute.
- Ramp commitment: guaranteed dedicated slots for the first 90 days of go-live and a 2-week priority runway for capacity spikes.

I’ve attached a short proposal and a draft mutual action plan. If that looks ok, we can schedule a 30-min technical kickoff with Marissa (ops) and Naomi (CS) later this week.

Thanks —
Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0124

Attachments: redwood-scale-commitment-v2.pdf
From: Elena Marsh <elena@highcrest.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Omar Singh <omar.singh@highcrest.io>, procurement <procurement@highcrest.io>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & scale commitment — Highcrest

Thanks Jordan.

Short version: we are reopening the renewal because the other provider claims they can offer 40% savings at scale and will run a bake-off next month. Procurement wants clear benchmarks and an ops proof that your service can hold latency at higher throughput. Two asks before we commit to a side-by-side:

1) Can you provide a 7-day throughput/latency snapshot against a production-like prompt mix? (we need p50/p90/p99 for 1k/5k/10k concurrent sessions)
2) Security/compliance artifacts — SOC2 summary + retention guarantees for request logs.

If you can meet those, I’ll push procurement to accelerate. Otherwise we’ll proceed with the competitive eval.

—Elena
Head of Product Operations | Highcrest
elena@highcrest.io
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Highcrest renewal — urgent benchmark request

Marissa / Naomi — forwarding Elena's note. Highcrest is clarifying requirements and procurement needs artifacts. Can we:

- Marissa: spin up a 7-day dedicated run using their sample prompt set (I will share logs). We need p50/p90/p99 for 1k/5k/10k concurrent sessions. Include the quantization profile and kernel config used.
- Naomi: pull SOC2 summary and a short note on retention guarantees + audit logs.

Attachments: Highcrest_MVP-benchmark-sprint-plan.xlsx (contains their sample prompt mix + target SLAs).

This is time-sensitive — Elena said procurement will make a decision within 10 business days.

Jordan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Highcrest renewal — urgent benchmark request

Jordan — on it. Quick summary of what we can deliver and constraints:

- We will run a controlled 7-day throughput test in a dedicated cluster (N2 GPUs) using the provided prompt mix. Expect p50/p90/p99 numbers for token generation and end-to-end latency.
- Preliminary projection: with their 10k concurrent sessions profile, we can sustain ~6k TPS with p99 < 450ms using mixed-precision q4f16 and our batching config (batch-window=8ms). Will confirm actuals after run.
- We’ll produce a single CSV of raw logs (attachment: Highcrest_Q2_throughput_logs.csv) and a concise PDF summary for procurement.
- Also note: if they require a warm KV cache warm-start (hot prefix), latency improves ~20% — include warm cache procedure in the report.

ETA: initial logs + summary by Thu EOD (24 Jun). I’ll also add the exact runtime kernel matrix used.

Marissa
Senior Ops Lead | Redwood Inference

Elena — thanks for the clarity. We’ll do the 7-day run and share artifacts. To move quickly I propose the following mutual action plan:

1) Redwood runs the 7-day dedicated benchmark (Marissa) and shares raw logs + summary by Thu EOD (24 Jun).
2) Highcrest grants a 48-hour side-by-side window the week of Jul 11 — Redwood will cover compute and provide identical input streams.
3) If Redwood meets the agreed p99/p90 targets, we sign a 12-month renewal with a committed-capacity uplift (6 months prepay option) — price protection for 12 months and a 15% uplift discount on reserved capacity.
4) Procurement review: Naomi will provide SOC2 summary and a one-page retention SLA that meets your legal team's needs.

I’ve attached the updated commitment terms and the DocuSign link to the initial SOW. If you approve, we can start the technical run today.

DocuSign: https://signin.docusign.com/Envelope/ABC123
Drive (raw logs): https://drive.google.com/highcrest-quarterly-analysis

Best,
Jordan

Jordan / team — appreciate the fast turnaround and the mutual action plan. Procurement will start a parallel review but we’re happy to run the 48-hour side-by-side week of Jul 11. Before that, two items:

- Please upload the 7-day raw logs to the Drive link you shared and include the kernel/config manifest (Marissa).
- Procurement wants the DocuSign SOW routed to procurement@highcrest.io and a plain-language memo of the retention window (Naomi).

We’ll confirm the side-by-side time slot by Friday. If results look as you project, I’ll push to keep Highcrest on Redwood and speed up approvals.
